# Plan: Unattended SPE rounds r05 and later (overnight)

## What I need from you before you go

You did not give me a round cap or a budget cap. The loop rules require one, so I will use the defaults below. Change them now if they are wrong. If you approve without changes, these defaults apply.

| Limit | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Round cap | 4 rounds (r05 to r08) | This leaves enough rounds to see a trend. It also limits how far the design can drift without you. |
| Total spend cap | 4 times the measured cost of r04 | This is about one r04-sized round per slot. I do not have a measured dollar figure for later rounds yet. |
| Per-round spend cap | 1.5 times the measured cost of r04 | A round that costs more than this is doing something I did not predict. |
| Clock cap | No new round starts after 06:00 local time | You will have a finished, committed report when you wake up. |

## Ground rules for the night

- I commit locally after each SPE step on the current branch. I do not push, open PRs, deploy, or send any message. The commits carry no Claude attribution.
- I approve my own plan for each round. So every prediction is committed in `SPE rNN predict` before any harness change or trial runs. You can then check with git that no prediction was edited after the results came in.
- The author does not touch the judge. I change graders only in the specify step, before predicting. I never loosen a grader to make a prediction hit.
- If I find a grader bug after a run, I log it in `spe/failures.md`. I keep the original numbers next to any regraded numbers in the log.
- I keep every requirement that came from your words. I can add requirements that come from failure IDs or from round evidence. I cannot drop or weaken a requirement you set.
- Each round makes at most one change to the system under test. More changes in one round make a miss impossible to explain.

## What I may change without you, and what I may not

| I may change these on my own | I stop and wait for you on these |
|---|---|
| Add harder tasks when every configuration passed everything | Any change to a requirement sourced from you |
| Tighten a grader, with a failure ID as the source | Raising any cap |
| Fix a harness bug and log it as a failure entry | Switching the model under test, or adding a new model |
| Apply one item from the last round's "Proposed for round N+1" table | Any change that touches an external system, account, or system of record |
| Adjust trial count inside the per-round spend cap | A go-live call, or removing a configuration from the comparison |

## Round 5

### 1. Specify

- I start from the "Proposed for round 5" table that r04 learn wrote into `spe/spec/spec.md`.
- I pick one proposal. I prefer the one tied to the largest r04 miss or the most frequent failure ID.
- I update the requirement table. Each new row has an ID, the requirement, a source (an r04 failure ID or an r04 decision), and a test.
- No new transcript exists for this round because you are asleep. I save your instruction from tonight as `spe/spec/transcripts/r05.md` and note that the round runs unattended.
- Commit: `SPE r05 specify: <the one change and its failure ID>`.

### 2. Predict

- I start from `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml`, which r04 learn wrote from the measured r04 values.
- I fill one number per metric and configuration. Each number gets a stated error band, a one-line Why, and the grader check that measures it.
- I add the "same as last round" column using the r04 measured values. This column is the naive guess my predictions have to beat.
- I give a cost and time estimate for the run and label it unmeasured.
- I save `spe/plans/r05.md` and `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` and remove the draft status.
- Commit: `SPE r05 predict: <one-line headline prediction>`. No harness work or trial starts before this commit.

### 3. Evaluate

- I build or update `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`. These gates must pass before the real run:
  1. The harness loads and lists the expected configurations and tasks.
  2. No answer key, grader file, or expected output is reachable from a trial's workspace or prompt.
  3. Each grader passes a known-good sample and fails a known-bad sample.
  4. A dry run with one trial per configuration completes and grades cleanly.
  5. The projected cost of the full run is under the per-round cap.
- Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (harness): <what changed>`.
- I launch the Workflow. It returns at launch, so I wait for its completion notice before grading.
- I write the graded output to `spe/evals/results/r05/`.
- Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline numbers>`.

### 4. Learn

- I add the r05 section to `spe/prediction-log.md`. It has Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer columns.
- Under the table I write "Which Why broke". For each miss I quote the Why and name the wrong assumption.
- If the naive guess was closer than my predictions, I say so plainly.
- I add new failure types to `spe/failures.md`, continuing the F numbering.
- I add a "Proposed for round 6" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- I update `spe/README.md` with a one-paragraph result and the rerun command.
- Commit: `SPE r05 learn: <hit count and main finding>`, then tag `spe-r05`.

## Rounds 6 to 8

Each round repeats the four steps above, starting from the previous round's proposals and draft prediction. Before each specify step I check every stop and halt rule below. If none fires, I start the next round.

## When I stop (normal end)

- Predictions hit within their stated error for 3 rounds in a row. I count r03 and r04 toward this if their verdicts were all hits. I then report that the design is stable enough for you to judge go-live. I do not make the go-live call.
- The round cap, total spend cap, or clock cap is reached.
- Two rounds in a row have every configuration passing everything, even after I added harder tasks. More rounds would measure nothing until you decide what "harder" should mean.

## When I halt mid-round

I halt the round, commit what exists with a `SPE rNN halted: <reason>` message, and stop the loop if any of these happen:

- A spend cap is hit.
- An answer key or grader output leaks to a trial.
- A grader is found broken during the run.
- A failure needs a decision from the table above that only you can make.
- The Workflow errors twice in a row on the same step.

## What you will find in the morning

- Local commits and `spe-rNN` tags for each finished round. Nothing is pushed.
- A short report in chat with these parts:
  1. One headline line per round with its key measured numbers.
  2. The prediction accuracy trend per round. This is the hit count, and whether my predictions or the naive guess was closer.
  3. Which stop or halt rule ended the night.
  4. Open decisions for you, each with the evidence and the round it came from.
  5. Total spend against the cap, with the measured cost of each round.
